title: בר אדא משוחאה

paragraphs: Bar Adda Meshucha'ah means a land surveyor, as the Arukh explains. A marginal gloss to Yalkut, Mas'ei, explains a place name. Rav Yehudah told Rav Adda Meshucha'ah, “Be careful with measurement,” Bava Metzia 107b: this supports the Arukh. Eruvin, chapter 5, 56b: Rava said, “Bar Adda Meshucha'ah explained to me,” concerning measuring boundaries. Rashi: he marks the city’s boundaries; Bar Adda is a man’s name. End quotation. I do not understand “Bar Adda is a man’s name”: it implies his name was Bar Adda. If he meant Adda is a man’s name, that is obvious—there are many Addas. If Bar Adda was his name, whence is this known? Perhaps bar means son of Adda.
